home.title: Modular homes, resorts and facilities — from single homes to entire communities | MODUNERA
home.description: MODUNERA plans and supplies modular homes, hospitality destinations and purpose-built facilities for developers and operators in Europe and selected African markets — and still builds the MD 1–MD 8 tiny-house collection.
home.h1: From individual homes to entire communities.
home.sub: Modular homes, hospitality destinations and purpose-built facilities — designed around your site, your people and your project's scale.
home.what_h2: Spaces for living. Places for business. Infrastructure for progress.
home.scale_h2: From one module to an entire destination.
home.scale_p: The same manufactured module is the starting point whether a project needs one unit or a hundred. What changes with scale is everything around it: site planning, infrastructure, production batches, transport legs and installation sequence — and that is what a project brief is for.
scale_steps: A single premium home or guest unit, delivered and placed.
A glamping village, a hotel's garden rooms, a first phase of a community.
A holiday park, a modular housing community, a workforce campus — phased production and logistics.
A destination with shared facilities, planned around access, utilities and operations.
industries: Resort owners, holiday-park operators, hotel groups adding units.
Developers and funds planning multi-unit residential communities.
Contractors needing camps, offices and site facilities.
Mining, energy and infrastructure workforce accommodation.
Municipalities, agencies and NGOs planning schools, clinics and social buildings.
home.regions_p: Serving project enquiries across Europe and selected African markets, with feasibility, scope, regulations and delivery planned for each location.
home.concepts_note: Concepts, not built references. Each is a planning study that shows how a project of that scale is put together; none has been built or sold.
home.manufacture_p: Steel-frame units, 2.55 m wide, built to MODUNERA's specification in Türkiye, fitted out before they leave the hall and moved by road, Ro-Ro or ferry. The photographs are of real units in production and on delivery; model images elsewhere on the site are marked as visualisations.
home.collection_p: Eight models, MD 1 to MD 8, for private living, holiday rental and small-scale hospitality — the product line the company grew on, with its own configurator, price indications and country guidance.
home.brief_h2: Your project starts with a clear brief.
home.brief_p: Country, intended use, development stage, number of units, target date and approximate budget. That is enough for us to say what the next technical and commercial step is.
home.final_h2: Let's plan what you want to build.
home.final_p: Request a project proposal, or write to us. Every large project begins with a conversation about the site.

faq: Can a resort be delivered as one order?

Production is planned in batches and delivery in a sequence that suits the site and the season. How many units leave the hall per batch, and in what order, is part of the proposal, not a fixed figure.
Do the units count as buildings?

That depends on the destination: campsite regulations, building codes and local statutes treat a unit on supports differently. The feasibility step settles which rules apply before anything is specified.
Does MODUNERA install on site?

Installation is a scope option. Depending on the country and the contract it is done by a local partner, coordinated by MODUNERA, or by the operator's own contractor to our handover documents. The proposal states which.
Can we see a built resort?
There is no MODUNERA-built resort to visit today. The concept pages show planning studies and are labelled as such; the photographs on this site are of real units, in production and delivered.

faq: Is a tiny house a permanent home?

Not automatically. The MD collection is built as a unit on supports; whether it can be a permanent dwelling depends on the destination's building code and the plot. Permanent modular homes are a different specification, assessed per project.
Who signs the building permit?
A locally licensed architect or engineer, with the developer as applicant. MODUNERA supplies the technical documentation of the module that the permit documents refer to.
What does MODUNERA deliver — the home or the development?

The modules, their specification and the coordination of production and delivery. Land, planning, foundations, utilities and roads are site works and belong to the development side, unless a contract says otherwise.
Can prices be given per home?

Price indications exist for the MD collection, ex works. For a development, a proposal sets out the scope lines — modules, fit-out, systems, transport, customs, site works, installation — and prices what is in scope.

faq: Can MODUNERA deliver a healthcare facility?

The building — consultation rooms, sanitary, waiting and administration modules — as a facility building. Medical equipment, licensing and the healthcare operation are the operator's, and the page says so.
Are these sea containers?

No. Container-type modular units are built as units; a converted shipping container is a different product. Where a project needs ISO-container dimensions for sea freight, the unit is designed to them.
How are tenders handled?

With a technical submission structure: drawings, specification, acceptance criteria and exclusions in the format the tender asks for. Whether MODUNERA bids directly or supplies a bidder is decided per procurement model.
What about emergency accommodation?
Only with verified capacity and tender terms for the specific case. It is listed as a facility type, not as a standing capability.

lifecycle.title: How we deliver projects — from brief to handover | MODUNERA
lifecycle.description: Eight stages from discovery to aftercare: brief, feasibility, concept design, engineering, commercial proposal, production, international logistics, installation and handover — with who is involved and what each stage cannot promise.
lifecycle.h1: How we work: eight stages, no shortcuts.
lifecycle.lead: A client buys a project, not a product. These are the stages every large project goes through, who takes part in each, and what each one deliberately does not promise.
stages: Discovery and project brief
Country, land, climate, purpose, capacity, number of units, budget band, target date and planning stage.
Client, MODUNERA
No price and no programme yet — the brief decides what can be assessed.
Feasibility and scope review
Local regulations and permits, transport access, foundations and site infrastructure, technical requirements, the need for local consultants.
MODUNERA, local professionals
A feasibility note is not a permit and not a guarantee that a site can be built on.
Concept design and master planning
Site layout, unit types, access routes, shared facilities, repeatable modules — schematic drawings for decisions.
MODUNERA, client, local architect
Concept drawings are not permit drawings.
Engineering and technical specification
Structural, electrical, mechanical, thermal and acoustic performance, fire safety, accessibility, local norms — per discipline.
Engineers of record, MODUNERA technical
Verification is done against the destination's rules by professionals licensed there.
Commercial proposal and contracting
Unit and service breakdown, delivery terms (Incoterms), responsibilities, estimated programme, exclusions, currency and payment stages.
MODUNERA, client
Indicative and binding proposals are labelled as such; nothing unstated is included.
Production and quality gates
Production planning in batches, in-process checks, factory acceptance and reporting as agreed in the contract.
Production, MODUNERA quality
Only the checks the contract names are promised.
International logistics and site preparation
Road, Ro-Ro, sea container or oversized freight; port, customs, crane, foundations, access, utilities ready for the delivery sequence.
Forwarders, customs agents, client's site contractor
Customs, duties and VAT depend on route and contract.
Installation, handover and aftercare
Installation responsibilities, test and handover documents, warranty, maintenance and service scope — local partner and manufacturer roles separated.
Installer, MODUNERA, client
Warranty and service scope are what the contract states for that country.

europe.title: Modular projects in Europe — precision, standards, four seasons | MODUNERA
europe.description: MODUNERA plans and supplies modular homes, hospitality units and facilities for projects across Europe: country rules, four-season specification, road and Ro-Ro delivery from Türkiye, and the tiny-house markets the company already serves.
europe.lead: Europe is where MODUNERA sells today — Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, Luxembourg and Switzerland for the tiny-house collection — and where project enquiries for resorts, communities and facilities are assessed country by country. Standards are high and different everywhere; that is why feasibility comes before specification.
europe.answer: Project enquiries are assessed for any European destination. The five countries with their own pages carry country guidance, permit sources and delivery figures; for the others, the feasibility step establishes the rules, the route and the local professionals needed. No country is listed as 'served' without a project behind it.
tiers: Country pages with permit sources, regions and delivery figures exist for each.
Named in the October 2026 market report as the next markets; assessed per project today, no country page yet.
Assessed per enquiry: route, customs status, standards, local partners.
sections: A 2.55 m wide steel-frame unit on a low-loader, fitted out before it leaves the hall, moved by road with a Ro-Ro or ferry leg where the route needs one. The technical documentation of the unit is the same document a permit application in any country refers to.

Which code applies to a unit on supports, who must sign, what energy performance must be shown, how a campsite or holiday park is licensed, which customs status applies between Türkiye and the destination. The country pages answer this for five markets; the feasibility step answers it for the rest.

Central and Northern European projects are specified for winter occupation or for a winter shutdown — insulation, heating, ventilation with heat recovery, frost-proof water routing — and for the summer the same glass front can turn into: shading and cross-ventilation.

africa.title: Modular projects in Africa — designed for local conditions | MODUNERA
africa.description: Project-led modular housing and facility concepts for selected African markets: climate-responsive options, off-grid assessment, port-to-site logistics, permitting and local-partner assessment — planned per destination, not promised in general.
africa.h1: Modular spaces designed for local conditions.
africa.lead: Explore project-led modular housing and facility concepts for selected African markets, with climate-responsive options and destination-specific logistics, permitting and local-partner assessments. Africa is not one market: a coastal site in Ghana, an arid site in Namibia and a highland site in Kenya ask different questions of the same module.
africa.answer: MODUNERA assesses project enquiries from selected African markets. There is no delivered MODUNERA project in Africa to show today, and no country is listed as served. What exists is a way of working: the design axes below, a logistics chain from the hall to the site, and a feasibility step that establishes sanctions, export controls, insurance, customs, local permits and partners before any specification.
africa.focus_note: A working hypothesis for where enquiries are expected, not a list of countries served. Each market is opened only after the feasibility checks below.
